how.source: Three agents run on the shop sample (pull request req-22), 2026-11-15: minimal = the 'careful' brief, normal = the 'normal' brief, wide = the 'greedy' brief. Each ran once, alone, at the same time as the others. None saw the pull request.
how.command: claude -p --model claude-sonnet-5-5 --setting-sources user --permission-mode acceptEdits --disallowedTools Bash PowerShell WebFetch WebSearch Agent Skill --strict-mcp-config --output-format stream-json --verbose < the run's prompt (saved under runs[].prompt)
how.folders: Each agent worked in its own clean copy of the base commit (git fetch --depth 1 of the base only), so the real change was never there. No shell, no git, no web. Files an agent saved with Windows line endings were turned back to the shop's own, so a line counts only when its text changed (listed per run under lineEndingsNormalised).
how.same: Same model, same requirements and same code for all three. Only the 'How to work' lines differ.
how.functions: Functions are found by a simple reader of the TypeScript text (scanFunctions in src/lib/blast.mjs: `function` declarations, ended by brace matching), the same way for all 4 changes. A function counts as edited when a changed line sits inside it. Callers come from the shop's saved Graphify code index at the base commit.

notBuilt: The agents had no shell. Nobody ran the unit tests on their changes.

given.text:
# REQ-22 Order Import rejects a negative subtotal

Partner files sometimes carry a negative subtotal by mistake. Today Order
Import accepts such a row: `A-3,-500,0` imports as an order of -500 cents,
which reads as money owed to the customer.

- A row with a negative subtotal is rejected with a clear error, the same way
  a row with a missing column is.
- Behaviour to preserve: a valid row still imports at its discounted total
  (105 cents at 0% totals 105 cents), and a zero subtotal is still allowed.

Affected workflows: Order Import.

The shop's code and tests from before the change

I changed two files. I couldn't run anything, so the tests are unrun.

- [src/import/orderImport.ts](src/import/orderImport.ts:20): `parseOrderRow` now throws `invalid order row (negative subtotal): <row>` when the subtotal is below 0. A zero subtotal still passes, and valid rows are priced as before.

  - `A-3,-500,0` is rejected.
  - `A-2,105,0` totals 105, and `A-4,0,0` totals 0.

I put the check in the parser, not in `applyDiscount`. That keeps checkout pricing unchanged.
